title: HomeFlood Deposit Difference — How a First Payment Above or Below the Down Share Is Settled
content:
**Definition.** The deposit difference of a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies term is the payments received for the term as its installment 1, less the sum of two things: the tier's policy fee, and the plan's down share of the booked term premium item.

| Plan | Down share of the booked term premium item |
|---|---|
| QUARTERLY | 40 percent |
| semi-annual | 50 percent |

**Settlement of the difference.**

| Installments of the term still to come (the plan's installments not yet received) | The deposit difference |
|---|---|
| three or more | is spread equally over them; this installment gives back one equal part |
| one or two | is given back in full by the next installment |
| none | is settled separately and not through an installment |

**Direction.** "Giving back" lowers the installment due by the part concerned. A negative deposit difference — a first payment short of the policy fee and down share — raises the installment due by that part instead.

**The installment's term.** The installment's term is the term of the latest first payment (installment 1) received on the policy.

**Installments still to come.** The installments of a term are its first payment and, after it, three later installments due 3, 6 and 9 calendar months after the term start on QUARTERLY, or one later installment due 6 calendar months after the term start on the semi-annual plan. The installments still to come are those of the plan not yet received: the plan's number of installments (4 on QUARTERLY, 2 on the semi-annual plan) less the payments received for the term.

## Hypothetical cases

- **Spread over three.** QUARTERLY, booked term premium item 1,850.00, policy fee 35. The down share is 740.00, so with the fee 775.00 was expected. A first payment of 805.00 leaves a deposit difference of 30.00. Only the first payment has been received, so three installments are still to come, and this installment gives back 10.00.
- **Next installment in full.** The same policy with two installments already received has two still to come. The next installment gives back the full 30.00.
